rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a TiN diffusion barrier interlayer between the substrate and Cr coating, whereas the paper uses an AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy alloy coating with varied Al content and no interlayer. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies PWR subcritical water (~315°C) and accident steam (~1200°C), while the paper uses isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000°C and 1100°C. The temperature ranges and environments differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on a TiN barrier to suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion, while the paper's mechanism involves Al content tuning to form a protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 oxide layer and avoid detrimental intermetallics. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interdiffusion and maintained oxidation resistance for a Cr/TiN system, whereas the paper predicts and measures an optimal Al content (~10 at.%) minimizing oxidation rate in a high-entropy alloy coating. The predicted properties and systems differ.
